completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented lint-hook-registration-paths.sh (four checks: CWD-relative path shape in settings surfaces and markdown registration templates, fragment coverage of install-once root-files registrations, existence of every source-store-resolvable invoked script), its 18-assertion both-polarity fixture suite, and wired it as verify-deploy.sh gate 21 (--only-gate range widened 1-20 -> 1-21). All six plan phases closed (five COMPLETED, Phase 6 COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS for one unrelated, concurrently in-flight task's orphan files); all twelve dispatch acceptance criteria verified with concrete evidence.

memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's gate 8 (tests/run-all.sh) is not safely wall-clock-predictable: at least one test fixture (the anti-recursion probe used by test-deploy-verify-wiring.sh / test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh) invokes verify-deploy.sh AGAIN from inside gate 8's own run-all.sh pass, and that nested invocation's own run-all.sh is forced to JOBS=1 by the RUN_ALL_NESTED guard. A single top-level `bash verify-deploy.sh .` (no --skip-slow) can therefore take several times longer than its documented ~10 minute solo baseline, with no visible symptom other than gate 8 appearing to hang.

When extracting an invoked shell-script path from a JSON hook-registration command string with a bash word-split (`read -ra words <<< "$text"`), always strip trailing shell metacharacters (`;`, `)`, `,`, `}`) from the candidate token before testing its file-extension suffix (e.g. `.sh`). A realistic command string can abut a script path directly against punctuation with no intervening whitespace (`bash foo.sh; fi'`), and an extension-suffix test without this strip silently misses such tokens.

To get a conclusive verify-deploy.sh full-battery result without hitting gate 8's nested-invocation slowdown (see the sibling INSIGHT on gate 8), run `verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow` (covers every gate except 8, completes in roughly a minute) and then `tests/run-all.sh --jobs auto --fail-on-new` directly and separately (not nested inside another verify-deploy.sh call) for gate 8's own suites. --fail-on-new classifies each failing suite as EXPECTED (matches tests/known-failures.txt) or NEW, so a clean run shows exactly which failures (if any) are this change's regression versus pre-existing. This two-call pattern finished in under 10 minutes total where a single un-skip-slow invocation previously ran past a 45-minute wait budget without concluding.

A `verify-deploy.sh` gate failure is not automatically this task's regression: before fixing it, check `git log --oneline -- <path>` for the finding's named file(s). If the most recent commits touching them belong to a differently-themed, concurrently in-flight task (visible by commit message prefix/topic, not this task's own number), the failure likely traces to that task's unfinished deployment/cleanup rather than to the change under test. Reproduce the specific gate standalone (e.g. `--only-gate N`) to confirm the failure is independent of your own changes, then record it as a plan Reasoned Exclusion with the evidencing commands rather than fixing files outside your own file_scope -- fixing them risks overwriting the other task's in-flight work.
